anne: Heads-up — since the kernel-selector tweak yesterday I'm seeing p99 tail spikes for streaming chat at 95% load. Non-streaming completions look fine. Anyone else see the same? :thinking:
sourabh: saw a couple alerts, didn't dig in yet. Can you paste the perf trace?
anne: pasted flamegraph in #temp, but TL;DR: tail latency jumps ~220ms at p99 when mb_size >= 6 for streaming. p95 unaffected. throughput improves but SLA violation windows open.
mike: interesting, could be handshake vs steady-state scheduling divergence. Streaming keeps KV cache hot but kernel switch may be introducing extra serialization. Did you capture kernel selection trace?
anne: yes — attached snippet: ```kernel_selector.log
[2026-02-10T12:03:45Z] session_id=abcd kernel_choice=optim_kv_fast seq_len=64 mb=6
[2026-02-10T12:03:45Z] session_id=abcd kernel_choice=scalar_fallback seq_len=64 mb=6 reason=kv_eviction
```
jess: that reason=kv_eviction stands out. If the selector flips mid-request we can add tail work. We saw similar pattern in a different reg where kv spill caused micro-kernel fallbacks.
sourabh: I ran a quick microtrace — when mb_size grows we keep more concurrent contexts and that bumps KV pressure. Eviction -> kernel fallback -> more CPU work -> queueing -> p99 spike.
anne: can we avoid kernel flip for streaming at the handshake? Maybe force kernel_hint=optim_kv_fast until handshake completes, then let selector roam. Would that bias wrong for long sequences?
mike: we can try a hysteresis window: don't change kernels for X ms after first token emitted. Add a handshake grace to the selector to prefer current kernel. Tradeoff: may keep suboptimal kernel for some tail cases but reduces flips.
jess: also test lowering mb_target for streaming only — make streaming default mb_target=4 and completions keep mb_target=8. That keeps latency SLO while preserving throughput on batch workloads.
anne: trying two quick experiments now: 1) selector_hysteresis_ms=80, 2) streaming_mb_target=4 override. Will run A/B for 30m each against canary pool.
perf-bot: experiment scheduled: canary/streaming-hysteresis (80ms) vs canary/streaming-mb4. Link: https://perf.internal/runs/3523456789
sourabh: note: also add a KV stats probe to sample eviction counts per-second. Need that to correlate spike windows.
mike: if hysteresis helps, follow-up work should be to teach selector to consider "handshake in-flight" as a feature (avoid flips while kv locality unstable).
anne: update: after 30m, hysteresis reduced p99 spikes by ~45% but increased avg latency by 8ms. mb_target=4 kept p99 near baseline and lost ~12% throughput. Seems like the safer immediate fix is streaming_mb_target=4. We should still pursue selector-hysteresis for a cleaner long-term fix. :thumbsup:
sourabh: filing a follow-up RFC for selector-hysteresis + telemetry. I'll attach KV eviction probe patchset.
anne: awesome — thanks all. I'll roll the streaming_mb_target=4 override to prod canary and monitor next 6h. If regressions clear, we'll ship.
perf-bot: canary roll started at 1767001285; will post updates every 30m.
